claims.claim_vi: SWIFT is the main secure messaging system that links the world's banks; it is Belgium-based, run by its member banks and handles millions of payment messages per day.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Steps 1 to 5: Bank A sends the message to Regional Processor A; the regional processor validates the format and sends it to Slice Processor A, which stores it and tells the regional processor; the regional processor sends ACK or NAK to Bank A (ACK means the message will be sent to Bank B, NAK that it will not).
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Steps 6 to 12: Slice Processor A sends the message to Regional Processor B in London, which stores it temporarily, assigns a unique Message Output Number (MON) and sends it to Slice Processor B; Slice Processor B validates the MON and authorizes the regional processor to send the message; Bank B receives and stores it.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Steps 13 to 17: Bank B returns UAK (received without error) or UNK (checksum failure); Regional Processor B builds a report from the response and sends it to Slice Processor B, which stores it and sends a copy to Slice Processor A, which also stores it.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: The Regional Processor validates input messages and queues output messages; the Slice Processor stores and routes messages safely.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: That SWIFT carries instructions and not the money itself is general knowledge of the author; the source calls it a messaging system.
claims.verified_by: Author's general knowledge; not checked against SWIFT documentation.

design_notes_vi: Ba lược đồ nối nhau cho ba chặng của 17 bước (mỗi lược đồ tối đa ba bên), rồi một khung ghi ba điều cần nhớ. Mỗi lược đồ bắt đầu bằng bên đã xuất hiện ở cuối lược đồ trước.
source_deviations: Source lists 17 steps in one run; the lesson splits them into three sequences by the party that is active (sender side, crossing to London, receiver side).

The lesson points out that the sender's ACK arrives at step 5, before Bank B has the message, and so does not mean delivery; this follows from the source's own definition of ACK and is presented as such.
Steps 7 (temporary storage) and 9 to 10 (validation) are condensed into single messages in the figure; the text below the figure keeps them.
The lesson adds, as general knowledge, that SWIFT carries messages and the money settles elsewhere; the source only calls it a messaging system.
